label: Science fiction
title: Silence on the Calliope
premise: The Calliope research station has been circling in orbit for decades, patched up with tape, crammed with plants, cables and reheated coffee. Only a skeleton crew remains aboard, shut in with their experiments and their grudges, weeks away from the next freighter. Tonight, during the rest shift, someone never turned up for the handover.

art.style: retro-futurist 1970s science fiction concept painting, lived-in space station, worn beige plastic and scuffed metal, teal fluorescent light and warm amber glow, soft film grain, realistic proportions

victim.name: Miguel Ángel Torres
victim.description: A veteran of the space agency, he ran the Calliope with an iron fist and a paper notebook he never let out of his hand. Demanding, vindictive and brilliant, he knew every bolt on the station and every weakness of his crew.

people.name: Elena Vázquez
people.personality: Former test pilot, curt and disciplined. Says little, in short clipped sentences, as if every word cost oxygen. Keeps everyone at a formal distance and slips into radio jargon without noticing: ‘affirmative’, ‘negative’, ‘copy’. Never embellishes, distrusts people who talk too much, and only lets her pride show when someone questions her flying.
people.appearance: A woman in her early forties, angular face tanned by years in the cockpit, dark watchful eyes, very short black hair with a touch of grey at the temples. She wears a faded orange flight suit with agency patches, zipped up to the neck, and a pair of old headphones slung round her shoulders.

rooms.name: Command bridge
rooms.description: Curved beige plastic consoles surround a great window through which the Earth drifts slowly past, blue and enormous. Buttons blink amber, a continuous-feed printer hums in a corner, and the air smells of cold coffee and hot electrics.
ambience: As you step in, the radio on a console spits a crackle of static and falls silent again. Chipped mugs with names scrawled in marker go cold on the panels.
Every so often the Earth drags its blue light across the consoles and stains your hands. The printer swallows paper, stops, then hums again, as if having second thoughts.

rooms.name: Hydroponic greenhouse
rooms.description: Trays of lettuces and tomato plants climb towards violet grow lamps, and water drips ceaselessly through clear tubes. At the back, the air recyclers that keep the station breathable purr away, and the air is damp, warm and smells of wet earth.
ambience: As you step in, the warm air fogs your vision for a moment. A steady, almost musical drip sounds among the leaves, and it smells of basil and wet roots.
The violet lamps buzz at a pitch that gets into your teeth. On one tray someone has stuck a handwritten label: ‘Do not touch, they're growing’.

rooms.name: Cargo bay
rooms.description: A tall hangar full of containers lashed down with webbing, dominated by a yellow robotic arm folded beneath the ceiling. A metal catwalk runs along the walls high above the floor, and the airtight dock hatch seals off one end with black and yellow hazard stripes.
ambience: As you step in, the cold of the hangar creeps up your trouser legs. The straps creak with every turn of the station, and the echo hands each sound back a moment late.
It smells of rubber, packing dust and metal that never quite warms up. Under the ceiling, the robotic arm lets out the odd faint hydraulic click.

All you can hear is the hiss of the seals and the ticking of the compressors beyond the wall. The cold smells of clean metal and of nothing at all.

motives: Had falsified the radiation readings to cover up a leak in the generator. {victim} had found out and meant to report it to the agency in the next day's transmission.
Had secretly sold the experiment's results to a rival corporation. {victim} had the proof and meant to expose the sale before the agency board the next day.
Had hidden an illness at the medical check-up that rules out any further time in orbit. {victim} had found out and meant to order a compulsory return home on the next freighter.

Had skipped protocol during the last depressurisation, and a member of the previous crew died as a result. {victim} had pieced together what happened and meant to hand the report to the accident board the next day.
Had been siphoning off fuel and parts from the station to smuggle to the freighters. {victim} had found out and meant to report it to the orbital authority as soon as the next ship docked.
Had come aboard with a bought degree and an invented record. {victim} had discovered it and meant to send the full file to the agency the next day.

arrivals: The shuttle docks with a dull thud that runs through the whole structure. When the hatch opens, you're met by recycled air that smells of warm plastic and damp soil, and a corridor bathed in amber light that curves away out of sight.

From the window of the relief capsule you watch the Calliope grow: a ring of patched-up modules turning slowly against the blue of the Earth. After docking, the ring's gravity hands your weight back all at once, and your knees remind you that you're no longer at home.

You pass through the airlock amid hisses of pressure and warning lights that switch from red to green. On the other side, the station hums, drips and creaks like an old ship, and someone has stuck photos of beaches on the walls that nobody aboard will set foot on for a long time.

The trip from the launch platform lasted long enough for your coffee to go cold twice. Now you float for a moment in the docking bay, under greenish fluorescent tubes, until an invisible hand of gravity presses you to the Calliope's floor.
tensions: Up here there's nowhere to run: the next ship is weeks away and, until then, whoever did it is breathing the same air as you.
The recyclers hum on as if nothing had happened. From every hatch a member of the crew is watching you, and every one of them has some reason not to meet your eye.
Beyond the glass, the Earth keeps turning, indifferent. Inside, the silence weighs more than weightlessness, and someone is counting the minutes until you work it out.

night: The station passes into the dark side of its orbit, and the corridor lights dim to a rest-shift amber.
The recyclers change rhythm with a long sigh. In some module, someone puts on a pot of coffee that nobody ever pours.
A minor alarm beeps on a distant panel and switches itself off. Nobody in the crew goes to check it.
The general channel has been silent for a good while. All you can hear is the hull creaking as it cools and, now and then, a hatch hissing.
A shower of micrometeorites patters against the shielding like distant hail. The lights flicker and the whole station holds its breath.
The Earth begins to show at the edge of the windows. In the corridors, every closed hatch seems to hide someone listening.
epilogues: You gather the crew on the command bridge and set out the facts one by one, unhurried, while the printer hums in its corner. When you finish, nobody looks at {culprit}. {culprit}'s hands grip the edge of a console, then let go. The onboard computer confirms the order in its neutral voice and seals the hatches of the rest module: there {culprit} will wait until the next freighter docks. Through the great window, the Earth comes out of shadow and a thin dawn crosses the oceans.

There's no need to raise your voice. When you say {culprit}'s name, the silence on the Calliope grows so thick you can hear the recyclers from the far side of the ring. {culprit} offers no resistance. Two members of the crew escort {culprit} down the amber corridor, and the onboard computer closes the hatch with a hiss of pressure and logs it. In {scene}, someone finally switches off the lights. Outside, the station enters orbital day and the sun blazes against the panels.

When you finish laying out the case, {culprit} sinks into one of the orange vinyl armchairs in the dome and stares at the Earth for a long while. Nobody speaks. Over the general channel, the onboard computer announces that the module is sealed until the next freighter arrives and that the report is already on its way to the agency. Someone gathers up the pieces from the magnetic chessboard. As the sun peers over the rim of the planet, the Calliope keeps turning, a little quieter, and for the first time all night someone says {victim}'s name aloud.
